https://hungarytoday.hu/flydubai-restore.text: Flydubai Restores Budapest Service, with Daily Flights Planned for Winter Season Flydubai is resuming direct flights between Hungary and the United Arab Emirates. Starting July 31, the airline will once again operate flights from Dubai International Airport (DXB) to Liszt Ferenc International Airport in Budapest (BUD). Initially offering three flights per week, the service will be expanded to daily flights with the winter schedule. The Dubai-based airline is strengthening its presence in Central and Eastern Europe. By resuming direct flights to Budapest, the airline is responding to sustained high demand, which has grown steadily since it first entered the Hungarian market in 2021. During the peak season, the reactivated route serves vacationers, business travelers, and the important VFR (visiting friends and relatives) traffic in equal measure. For flydubai CEO Ghaith Al Ghaith, the return to the Hungarian capital is a clear commitment to the market. “The resumption of flights underscores our long-term investment in Hungary and reflects the strong economic and cultural ties between the two nations. Budapest remains one of our most important strategic markets in Europe,” he explained. The renewed service not only offers travelers in the region more choice but also strengthens Dubai’s role as a global hub for business and tourism. Jeyhun Efendi, Senior Vice President of Commercial Operations at flydubai, is optimistic about the upcoming season. As we approach the busy fall-winter travel season, this flight connection creates valuable new trade and tourism opportunities in both markets,” he emphasized. For passengers from Hungary, the Dubai hub opens the door to the world. Dubai. Photo: flydubai Through the codeshare partnership with Emirates, travelers can seamlessly access flydubai’s global network with a single ticket and through-check baggage. This network now includes more than 120 destinations in the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and Southeast Asia—including popular long-haul destinations such as the Maldives, Thailand, Kenya, Sri Lanka, and Oman. The route will be served by a fleet of Boeing 737 aircraft. Passengers from Hungary will also benefit from flexible stopover options in Dubai, allowing them to explore the metropolis’s attractions, shopping districts, and family-friendly experiences. Photo: flydubai Flight operations will begin on July 31 with three weekly flights (Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays); starting October 25, 2026, the frequency will increase to one daily flight. The flight lands in Budapest at 9:40 p.m. and departs back to Dubai at 10:40 p.m. Fares from Budapest: Round-trip flights in Business Class starting at 802,400 forints (2,231 euros), in Economy Class starting at 182,900 forints (509 euros). Fares from Dubai: Round-trip flights in Business Class starting at 15,585 UAE dirhams (3,733 euros), in Economy Class starting at 2,987 UAE dirhams (715 euros). The flights are now available for booking via the airline’s official website, the airline’s official app, and through affiliated travel agencies and sales partners. Photo: flydubai Since its launch in June 2009, flydubai has become a major player in the region’s aviation industry. With a modern, uniform fleet of 97 Boeing 737s (including 68 Boeing 737 MAX 8s and 3 MAX 9s), the airline connects destinations in 58 countries. A key feature of its strategy remains the development of underserved markets. More than 100 routes have been launched to destinations that previously had no direct connection to Dubai. Since its founding, the airline has carried over 137 million passengers. The direct flight reduces travel time to about 4.5 hours. Beállítom Egy 44 éves férfi meghalt, a hétéves fiát pedig súlyos sérülésekkel kellett kórházba szállítani szombaton a szlovéniai Bohinj községben, a Savica-vízezésnél – írja a Delo.si a hegyimentők és a rendőrség közleménye alapján. Kettejük közül először a fiú zuhant szakadékba, az apja pedig a segítségére akart sietni, amikor maga is lezuhant. A család a magyar turisták között is népszerű Savica-vizeséshez (Száva-vízeséshez) kirándult el, majd onnan visszafelé sétálva egy, a turistaútnál lévő pihenőhelyen állt meg. A hétéves gyerek itt eltávolodott a családtagjaitól, majd a körülbelül 60 méter mély szurdokba zuhant. A fiú zuhanás közben elsikoltotta magát, amit a családtagjai meghallottak, az apja pedig azonnal utánaindult. A sikoltásokat követve kereste a fiút, majd maga is belezuhant a szurdokba. A bohinji hegyimentők erről szóló Facebook-posztja szerint azzal hívták őket, hogy „gyerek zuhant a szakadékba”. Mivel több egységük a környéken gyakorlatozott, azonnal el tudtak indulni a Savica-vízesés felé és néhány perccel később már ott is voltak. A hegyimentők kötelekkel ereszkedtek a körülbelül 60 méter mély szurdokmederbe, ahol a fiút élve, de súlyos sérülésekkel, az apját azonban már holtan találták meg. https://www.dw.com/en/trump-grants-visa-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Oupf Prefer DW on Google Zohran Mamdani said he spoke with President Donald Trump on Saturday Image: NDZ/STAR MAX/IPx/picture alliance Advertisement New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Saturday that US President Donald Trump had agreed to grant a visa to the mother of a 15-year-old boy who was killed in a neighborhood in Bronx earlier this week. Javits Frimpong moved to New York from Ghana last year to be with his father and begin a new life in the US, according to Representative Ritchie Torres, a Democrat from the Bronx. Frimpong was shot in the abdomen on Thursday morning on his way to school and later died in the hospital, according to New York City police. There have been no arrests in the case so far, with police investigating the shooting. Mamdani says he spoke to Trump "I just got off the phone with President Trump and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately," Mamdani posted on X. "The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away," he wrote. "Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person." The killing led to an outpouring of grief in New York, with Torres writing, "Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him." The White House is yet to respond to the news. Teen was bullied in school, father says Thomas Frimpong remembered his son as a quiet boy, and said he was bullied at school. Ghana's Foreign Minister Sam Okudzeto Ablakwa thanked Mamdani and Trump in a post on X. He said Ghanaian officials were coordinating with Javits Frimpong's mother to assist her with the visa application process.
